comment: Declared divergences: a case listed here is allowed to disagree, for the recorded reason, and a case that STOPS diverging fails so the entry gets removed. Each entry cites the specification section or the measurement that settles it. Never used to silence a disagreement that has not been adjudicated.

functions.json:sum(//price).reason: XPath 1.0 §4.2 prints a number with as many digits as are needed to distinguish it from adjacent doubles, so 9.99 + 12.50 + 8.25 is 30.740000000000002 -- which both oracles produce. MFBASIC's toString(Float) is fixed at two decimal places, so the package can only say 30.74. Measured directly: a program printing toString(30.740000000000002) outputs 30.74, and toString(1.0/3.0) outputs 0.33. There is no float-formatting function with a precision argument (mfb man strings offers only padding; mfb man math offers round/ceil/floor). This is a limit of the language's number-to-text conversion, not of the XPath evaluator: the arithmetic itself agrees.
functions.json:sum(//price).settles: measured 2026-09-15; see packages/xml/README.md, 'Numbers are printed with two decimals'

operators.json:sum(//price).reason: The same case as functions.json:sum(//price) -- both corpus files ask it, because it is where the numeric formatting limit shows.
